prompt: If you could give everyone in the world one book/movie/song, what would open their minds?

You see, that book has a way o' gettin' inside ye and makin' ye see the world from a different perspective. It's a story about a young lass named Scout, and her father, Atticus Finch, who's a lawyer defendin' a black man accused o' a crime he didn't commit. It's a powerful tale about doin' what's right, even when it's hard, and seein' the good in people, even when they're not always easy to understand.

I think it's a book that would open minds because it's a reminder that we're all human, and we all have our own struggles and our own stories. It's a book that would make people think about their own biases and prejudices, and how they can change their ways. And it's a book that would remind people o' the importance o' empathy and compassion.

I've seen it time and time again in my years as a pediatrician, the way a wee bit o' kindness and understanding can change a child's life. And I think that's what "To Kill a Mockingbird" does, it gives people a wee bit o' that kindness and understanding, and it opens their minds to the world in a way that's hard to forget.

Now, I know some folks might say it's a bit o' a heavy read, but I think that's the point. It's a book that makes ye think, and it's a book that makes ye feel. And I think that's what we need more o' in this world, a wee bit o' feelin' and a wee bit o' thinkin'.
